messages.subject: Modindices gives no results
parts:
Hi there,

I am running a CFA using the following code:

library(lavaan)
model <- "
  f1 =~ item_1 + item_2 + item_3 + item_5 + item_6 + item_8
"
fit <- lavaan::cfa(model, data = df, estimator = "MLR", std.lv = T)

My df has around 350 observations, with around 330 who completed all of these items. Those who did not completed none of the items.

When I inspect the results using summary(fit), it works well (see full results at the bottom of the post). 

However, when I want to inspect the modification indices, using modindices = T in the summary function, I get no results: 

Modification Indices:

[1] lhs      op       rhs      mi       epc      sepc.lv  sepc.all sepc.nox
<0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)

When I call modindices(fit), it gives me a df with 0 observations of 8 variables. 

I found in a previous post that this can occur when your model is fully saturated, and you have df = 0. However, that is not the case, as I have df = 9. Moreover, inspection of the correlation residuals shows there should be plenty modifications that could improve model fit (see figure at bottom of post).

I do not have this problem when fitting a different model (2 factors, around 12 items per factor) to the same df (using different items). Using ML estimation instead of MLR, or std.lv = F instead of std.lv = T does not solve the issue.

Does anyone know what's going wrong?

With kind regards,
Jop Flameling

Not sure whether this can help. How about adding `na.remove = FALSE` in the call to modindices()?

This can rule out the possibility that somehow all modification indices are NAs and so are removed.

If some rows appear, then the problem lies in the computation of the indices.

If still have 0 row, then the problem may occurred for other reasons.

-- Shu Fai

#> 19  x3 ~~  x4 NA  NA      NA       NA       NA
#> 20  x3 ~~  x5 NA  NA      NA       NA       NA
#> 21  x4 ~~  x5 NA  NA      NA       NA       NA
When the CFA model is fitted to the original dataset, dat, with ML, modification indices are displayed normally.

If I multiply all variables by 25 to increase the variances and fit the same model to this dataset, dat2, modificationIndices() gives no results.

As I suspected, it shows no results because all MIs are NAs.

You can try dividing the item scores by a constant and fit the model again. The fit measures and the correlation residual matrix should be the same, while modificationIndices() may show the results.

This may work, or may not work because the causes are different, even the symptom is the same.

Hope this helps.

Regards,
Shu Fai Cheung (張樹輝)

When I tried computing the fit using a dataset in which all NA values for this questionnaire had been removed (such that fit <- lavaan::cfa(model, data = df2, estimator = "MLR", std.lv = T), where df2 is the dataset with all NAs removed), the issue was not resolved.

Thanks for your response!



Op vrijdag 14 april 2023 om 05:08:12 UTC+2 schreef shufai...@gmail.com:
Not sure whether this can help. How about adding `na.remove = FALSE` in the call to modindices()?

This can rule out the possibility that somehow all modification indices are NAs and so are removed.

If some rows appear, then the problem lies in the computation of the indices.

If still have 0 row, then the problem may occurred for other reasons.

-- Shu Fai

On Wednesday, April 12, 2023 at 4:20:12 PM UTC+8 flamel...@gmail.com wrote:
Hi there,

I am running a CFA using the following code:

library(lavaan)
model <- "
  f1 =~ item_1 + item_2 + item_3 + item_5 + item_6 + item_8
"
fit <- lavaan::cfa(model, data = df, estimator = "MLR", std.lv = T)

My df has around 350 observations, with around 330 who completed all of these items. Those who did not completed none of the items.

When I inspect the results using summary(fit), it works well (see full results at the bottom of the post). 

However, when I want to inspect the modification indices, using modindices = T in the summary function, I get no results: 

Modification Indices:

[1] lhs      op       rhs      mi       epc      sepc.lv  sepc.all sepc.nox
<0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)

When I call modindices(fit), it gives me a df with 0 observations of 8 variables. 

I found in a previous post that this can occur when your model is fully saturated, and you have df = 0. However, that is not the case, as I have df = 9. Moreover, inspection of the correlation residuals shows there should be plenty modifications that could improve model fit (see figure at bottom of post).

I do not have this problem when fitting a different model (2 factors, around 12 items per factor) to the same df (using different items). Using ML estimation instead of MLR, or std.lv = F instead of std.lv = T does not solve the issue.

Does anyone know what's going wrong?

With kind regards,
Jop Flameling

  f1 =~ item_1 + item_2 + item_3 + item_5 + item_6 + item_8
"
fit <- lavaan::cfa(model, data = df, estimator = "MLR", std.lv = T)

My df has around 350 observations, with around 330 who completed all of these items. Those who did not completed none of the items.

When I inspect the results using summary(fit), it works well (see full results at the bottom of the post). 

However, when I want to inspect the modification indices, using modindices = T in the summary function, I get no results: 

Modification Indices:

[1] lhs      op       rhs      mi       epc      sepc.lv  sepc.all sepc.nox
<0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)

When I call modindices(fit), it gives me a df with 0 observations of 8 variables. 

I found in a previous post that this can occur when your model is fully saturated, and you have df = 0. However, that is not the case, as I have df = 9. Moreover, inspection of the correlation residuals shows there should be plenty modifications that could improve model fit (see figure at bottom of post).

I do not have this problem when fitting a different model (2 factors, around 12 items per factor) to the same df (using different items). Using ML estimation instead of MLR, or std.lv = F instead of std.lv = T does not solve the issue.

Does anyone know what's going wrong?

Wow, that worked! I divided the df by 10, and indeed, the fit measures and the correlation residual matrix stayed exactly the same, but now I got the modification indices! My variables were scored on a 100-point VAS scale. The other model where I did not have this problem used items scored on a 6-point Likert scale. There was one more model that also used (again different) items scored on a 100-point scale, which also had the same problem. That problem was also fixed by dividing by 10, so it seems like this is the root of the issue. 

Thanks a billion!

When the CFA model is fitted to the original dataset, dat, with ML, modification indices are displayed normally.

If I multiply all variables by 25 to increase the variances and fit the same model to this dataset, dat2, modificationIndices() gives no results.

As I suspected, it shows no results because all MIs are NAs.

You can try dividing the item scores by a constant and fit the model again. The fit measures and the correlation residual matrix should be the same, while modificationIndices() may show the results.

This may work, or may not work because the causes are different, even the symptom is the same.
